title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

 lead : __NOTOC__

There are four **endings to *Dark Souls III***.

All four endings require the Ashen One to first gather the cinders of four great lords to reach the Kiln of the First Flame, where they must defeat the Soul of Cinder. Only the first ending does not require actions beyond strictly the main questline, although it is possible for up to three to be available simultaneously at the Kiln. All endings revolve around the First Flame, symbolized by a special bonfire that can be interacted with upon slaying the Soul of Cinder.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: Age of Dark
snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

The Ashen One, protagonist of *Dark Souls III*, is one of these Unkindled. After the Ashen One defeats each of the Lords of Cinder and places their remains upon their respective thrones in the Firelink Shrine, the Fire Keeper removes the embers of the Lords and bestows them upon the Ashen One, making them a "true lord, fit to link the fire," and imbuing them with the power to proceed to the Kiln of the First Flame.

 overview : The Fire upgrade path adds Fire Damage to all weapons, while removing all stat scaling bonuses. This makes Fire a good choice for lower level players, although the removal of scaling makes it a poor choice for those with high stats.

Several of Aldia's attacks deal mixed Fire and Dark damage, so some form of fire defense is recommended for this fight. All of his attacks deal either pure physical or Fire/Dark damage. The Fire Orbs have moderate tracking, so rolling may be needed to fully evade. Forbidden Sun can be cast in any direction, even directly behind him. The Fire Orb and Forbidden Sun attacks can be avoided by rolling, strafing around Aldia or running perpendicular to their trajectory.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

 lore : Aldia is the elder brother of King Vendrick, and aided his brother in founding the kingdom of Drangleic. He secluded himself in his manor, searching for secrets of life, viewing the Undead as the key to finding it. For his reverence of the Undead, Aldia was shunned by Vendrick, banished to his Keep forever. People who were invited to his manor commonly disappeared and were replaced with malformed beasts. The Southern and Northern Ritual Bands were created by Aldia and his acolytes after cruel, horrible experiments were performed on these people. Many valuable objects came out of Aldia's Keep, including the Sunset Staff, the Spitfire Spear, Soul Geyser, Unleash Magic, and Forbidden Sun.

Through his experiments, Aldia sought to learn the nature of the undead curse, and to shed the yoke of fate. He failed, however, and turned into a monstrosity, inhabiting the bonfires.

He was worshipped as the "God of the Darkmoon" and held the title of "God of the Dark Sun".

Despite being the son of Gwyn, Gwyndolin was born with a strong moon power, and "weak and repulsive" in appearance, particularly due to the snakes coiled around his lower half. Because of his darkmoon powers and his strong affinity for moon magic, as well as his lineage, Gwyndolin was raised as a female. While still young, Gwyn made him wear women's clothing and gave him a magic ring which would allow Gwyndolin to move and act in a feminine way, leading him to behave "like a dark and fleeting goddess".

 location : Dark Sun Gwyndolin guards the honorary tomb of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight in Anor Londo. The tomb can be found by using the spiraling staircase on the rotating bridge while the bridge is in its lowest position and descending to the second accessible bonfire. The player can then either pledge allegiance to him and his Blades of the Darkmoon or dare to trespass the fog door behind which he dwells, thus commencing the boss battle.

Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Gwyndolin's boss battle takes place in a seemingly never-ending corridor.

He is not a very difficult boss if the player has decent dodging skills. Of his three attacks, two can be avoided by hiding behind pillars, while the last one is more powerful and fast (he will tend to use the Sphere Shot after Orb Spread if the player is hiding behind pillars). The main issue in this fight is reaching him, as he will teleport away when the player approaches (equipping the Ring of Fog may increase the time available to attack before he teleports), meaning that the best time to run up to him is when he is just finishing off his Arrow Spread, as he takes a few moments to recover. Gwyndolin can still be damaged while he is in his teleporting animation and for a split second after actually moving, so it is possible to deal considerable damage at that moment.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Gwyndolin created an illusory image of his sister Gwynevere, to govern through her cherished figure and covering for her departure, taking upon himself to lead what remained of his father's kingdom and the Silver Knights through this illusion, though he didn't attempt to claim the throne for himself. Together they used the illusion of Gwynevere to seek a worthy champion to link the Flame again, creating a prophecy which they hoped to make self-fulfilling by guiding and manipulating those who passed their various challenges and earned the Lordvessel, a component required to access the Kiln of the First Flame, while also maintaining some semblance of divinity and control over the ancient city.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Despite his harsh upbringing, and having accepted his identity in the eyes of the other deities as fragile and repulsive, Gwyndolin would grow up with a deep admiration for his father and an aspiration to become like him, wearing a crown with the design of the sun that was imbued with his dark moon magic. He accepted his place and role to the point of supporting his father's will even after his death, and he took part in the workings of his kingdom. Although he was a deity of Anor Londo, Gwyndolin still grew into a powerful sorcerer, using a golden bow, infused with strong magic and employing arrows of moonlight, and even a catalyst for sorcery that channeled not the intelligence but the faith of the user. snippet: Possible relations between Gwyndolin and the Ringed City are unclear; although he is never directly mentioned within, and its inhabitants claim to serve Gwyn, there is a statue of Gwyndolin in a cathedral of the Ringed City.
